## Overview

The emerald ash borer spreads over long distances when people move infested
wood, founding outlier colonies far ahead of the main front. Once one is found,
what should be done there? @Mercader2011b took their model of local spread
(@Mercader2011; see the emerald ash borer vignette) and added three
treatments in a circle around the origin of an outlier:

- **ash reduction**: harvesting the large trees, removing their phloem and the
  larvae in it, once;
- **girdling**: girdling one large tree a cell each year, which draws egg-laying
  females to it, and destroying it with its larvae;
- **insecticide**: protecting the large trees with a systemic insecticide,
  which kills the larvae laid in them and keeps their phloem from being eaten.

Large trees (27.9 cm in diameter or more) hold half the phloem by default. The
authors also asked how the results change if females are drawn to stressed
trees.

This implementation is an **adaptation**: the authors' code was not available,
so the treatments are written from the text, with the gaps filled as the
deviations below list.

```{julia}
#| output: false
ENV["GKSwstype"] = "100"
using EcologicalCellularAutomata
using CellularAutomataCore
using Plots
```

## The treatments

The landscape is 101 × 101 cells of 50 m, each with 200 m² of ash phloem, with
100 adults released at the centre. Treated cells lie within a radius of the
origin. Without treatment the model is the base model with avoidance: its
radius of infestation after 15 years is 1350 m.

```{julia}
radii(sol) = [eab_spread(u).radius for u in sol.u]
simulate(; kw...) = solve(problem(:eab_management; kw...); saveat=1)
untreated = simulate()
radii(untreated)'
```

A girdled tree of 10.32 m² takes a share of the larvae laid in its cell given
by the ratio of the density of larvae on girdled to other trees. The source
fits that ratio as `20.468 x^-0.559` at a density `x` per m² on other trees,
from 16 outlier sites in Michigan; here it is capped at 20.468, its value at 1
larva per m². The ratio falls as density rises: in a cell of 200 m², a girdled
tree takes about half the eggs at the low densities ahead of a front, and 8%
where the phloem is full.

```{julia}
x = 0.5:0.5:88
y = min.(20.468 .* x .^ -0.559, 20.468)
share = 10.32 .* y ./ (10.32 .* y .+ (200 - 10.32))
plot(plot(x, y; ylabel="ratio, girdled to other trees"),
     plot(x, 100 .* share; ylabel="share in the girdled tree (%)", ylims=(0, 60));
     xlabel="larvae per m² of phloem", lw=2, legend=false, layout=(1, 2), size=(850, 320),
     left_margin=5Plots.mm, bottom_margin=5Plots.mm)
```

Under the **stress bias**, dispersing females favour cells with a girdled tree
(seven times as attractive) or stressed trees, whose attraction rises linearly
from 1 to 7 as the cell loses up to a third of its phloem.

## Treating within 300 m

The source's main comparison treats every cell within 300 m of the origin from
the start and follows the infestation for 15 years.

```{julia}
treatments = (:none, :girdling, :insecticide, :ash_reduction)
labels = ["standard" "girdled trees" "insecticide" "ash reduction"]
runs = Dict((tr, sb) => simulate(; treatment=tr, stress_bias=sb)
            for tr in treatments for sb in (false, true))
plot([plot(0:15, [radii(runs[(tr, sb)]) for tr in treatments]; label=labels,
           title=sb ? "stress bias" : "no stress bias", titlefontsize=10, xlabel="year",
           ylabel="radius of infestation (m)", lw=2, legend=:topleft, ylims=(0, 1500),
           color=[:black :gray :black :gray], ls=[:solid :solid :dash :dash])
      for sb in (false, true)]...; layout=(1, 2), size=(850, 380), left_margin=5Plots.mm,
     bottom_margin=5Plots.mm)
```

```{julia}
source = Dict((:none, false) => (1350, 5.45), (:girdling, false) => (1150, 4.45),
              (:insecticide, false) => (950, 3.3), (:ash_reduction, false) => (1350, 5.3),
              (:none, true) => (1100, 2.5), (:girdling, true) => (950, 2.1),
              (:insecticide, true) => (850, 1.8), (:ash_reduction, true) => (1150, 2.8))
[(; treatment=tr, stress_bias=sb, radius=Int(radii(runs[(tr, sb)])[end]),
  source_radius=source[(tr, sb)][1],
  beyond_millions=round(eab_beyond(runs[(tr, sb)].u[end], 300) / 1e6; digits=2),
  source_beyond=source[(tr, sb)][2])
 for sb in (false, true) for tr in treatments]
```

The radius after 15 years and the beetles beyond the treated area (millions),
against the source's Fig. 4 read by eye. As in the source:

- insecticide slows the spread most, then girdling;
- ash reduction does not reduce the beetles beyond the treated area;
- with the stress bias, ash reduction spreads faster than no treatment.

Insecticide is a little weaker here (1000 m against 950 without the bias) and
girdling a little stronger.

## The radius of treatment and the year it starts

The source then treated every cell out to radii of 0 to 1700 m, starting in
the first year or up to four years later, when an outlier might be found.

```{julia}
rs = 0:100:1700
starts = (0, 2, 4)
cases = [(tr, sb, st, r) for tr in (:girdling, :insecticide, :ash_reduction)
         for sb in (false, true) for st in starts for r in rs]
final = Vector{Float64}(undef, length(cases))
Threads.@threads for i in eachindex(cases)
    tr, sb, st, r = cases[i]
    prob = problem(:eab_management; treatment=tr, stress_bias=sb, start=st, radius=r)
    final[i] = eab_spread(solve(prob).u[end]).radius
end
sweep = Dict(cases .=> final)
plot([plot(rs, [[sweep[(tr, sb, st, r)] for r in rs] for st in starts];
           label=permutedims(["year $st" for st in starts]), lw=1.5,
           title="$(replace(String(tr), '_' => ' ')), $(sb ? "" : "no ")stress bias",
           titlefontsize=9, ylims=(600, 1650), xlabel="radius of treatment (m)",
           ylabel="radius after 15 years (m)", legend=:bottomleft)
      for tr in (:girdling, :insecticide, :ash_reduction) for sb in (false, true)]...;
     layout=(3, 2), size=(800, 860))
```

The results follow the source's Fig. 5:

- **Insecticide:** the radius falls to 800 m as the treated radius grows (750 m
  with the stress bias; the source has 800 and 700 m). Later starts weaken it.
- **Girdling:** the radius falls to 1100 m once the treated circle passes
  300–800 m, depending on the start, and stays there.
- **Under the stress bias:** girdling helps most at small radii and less at
  large ones, where the girdled cells draw beetles outwards, as the source
  found. Ash reduction widens spread as the treated circle grows, to
  1300–1450 m.

## How many trees can be treated

The source varied the share of the phloem in large trees, and so the share
that can be treated, from 0 to 90%. Here the whole lattice is treated.

```{julia}
shares = 0:0.1:0.9
share_cases = [(tr, sb, s) for tr in (:girdling, :insecticide, :ash_reduction)
               for sb in (false, true) for s in shares]
share_final = Vector{Float64}(undef, length(share_cases))
Threads.@threads for i in eachindex(share_cases)
    tr, sb, s = share_cases[i]
    prob = problem(:eab_management; treatment=tr, stress_bias=sb, share=s, radius=1700)
    share_final[i] = eab_spread(solve(prob).u[end]).radius
end
by_share = Dict(share_cases .=> share_final)
plot([plot(100 .* shares,
           [[by_share[(tr, sb, s)] for s in shares]
            for tr in (:girdling, :insecticide, :ash_reduction)];
           label=["girdled trees" "insecticide" "ash reduction"], lw=2,
           title=sb ? "stress bias" : "no stress bias", titlefontsize=10,
           xlabel="phloem available for treatment (%)",
           ylabel="radius after 15 years (m)", ylims=(0, 1700), legend=:bottomleft)
      for sb in (false, true)]...; layout=(1, 2), size=(850, 380), left_margin=5Plots.mm,
     bottom_margin=5Plots.mm)
```

Insecticide's effect grows steadily with the share treated, to 150 m at 90%,
as in the source's Fig. 3 (about 200 m). Girdling helps less, because each
cell girdles only one tree a year and the large trees run out. Ash removal
never slows the spread. Removing 75–90% of the phloem widens it here, which
the source does not show.

## The limits on girdling

Girdling is limited in two ways: only large trees can be girdled, and girdled
trees draw fewer eggs as densities rise. The source's Fig. 6 lifts each limit
in turn, girdling throughout the lattice.

```{julia}
scenarios = [("standard", (; treatment=:none)),
             ("all constraints", (; treatment=:girdling)),
             ("all phloem available", (; treatment=:girdling, share=1.0)),
             ("no reduction in attraction",
              (; treatment=:girdling, pmap=(; attraction_decline=false))),
             ("no constraints",
              (; treatment=:girdling, share=1.0, pmap=(; attraction_decline=false)))]
beetles = [[eab_spread(u).beetles / 1e6 for u in simulate(; radius=1700, kw...).u]
           for (_, kw) in scenarios]
plot(0:15, beetles; label=permutedims(first.(scenarios)), lw=2, xlabel="year",
     ylabel="beetles (millions)", legend=:topleft, size=(650, 360))
```

Each limit lifted cuts the population further. With neither, the
infestation stays small, as in the source.

## How stress is counted

The source counts a cell as stressed once a third of its "initial phloem" is
gone. Here that means phloem lost by any means. If only phloem eaten by
larvae counted, removing ash would leave the treated cells unstressed. Under
the stress bias it would then barely change the spread, unlike the source's
Figs. 3 and 5.

```{julia}
lost = [eab_spread(solve(problem(:eab_management; treatment=:ash_reduction,
                                 stress_bias=true, radius=r)).u[end]).radius
        for r in (0, 300, 800, 1700)]
eaten = [eab_spread(solve(problem(:eab_management; treatment=:ash_reduction,
                                  stress_bias=true, radius=r,
                                  pmap=(; stress_from=:eaten))).u[end]).radius
         for r in (0, 300, 800, 1700)]
(; radius_of_treatment=[0, 300, 800, 1700], any_loss=lost, eaten_only=eaten)
```
